takeaway: The small intestine secretes 1.5 L of fluid per day. Fluid balance for a nil-by-mouth patient must count absorption and secretion along the whole gut.

question.text: A patient is nil by mouth for several days. Which statement about fluid secretion and absorption in the gut is correct?

answer.text: The small intestine secretes 1.5 L of fluid per day.
answer.say: The small intestine secretes one and a half litres of fluid per day.

lines.text: Our patient will be nil by mouth for days, so we must plan his fluids carefully.
The gut both secretes and absorbs fluid all day long. The stomach secretes two to three litres of gastric juice.
The small intestine secretes one and a half litres of fluid per day. That is our answer.
(sigh) The large bowel absorbs one litre, so very little is left behind.
Only about a hundred millilitres leaves in the faeces.
So fluid balance must count every part of the gut, to keep a positive net balance.
